summary.headline: NPST Q1 FY27 revenue about INR 61.42 crore, roughly 75% YoY but down QoQ; management reiterates 60-70% FY27 growth and ~30% EBITDA margin guidance.
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue of about INR 61.42 crore, up about 75% YoY, with EBITDA up 66% and net profit of about INR 11.4 crore. Revenue fell sequentially from the record INR 68 crore in Q4 FY26, which management attributed to milestone-based recognition in a shifted business mix, with PPaaS cut to about 5% of projections. Management held FY27 guidance of 60-70% growth and around 30% EBITDA margin, and flagged MDR on UPI as a possible future revenue driver that is not yet quantified. International revenue is about 10-12% of consolidated revenue, and management targets around 50% over about two years.

financial_highlights.change: about +75% YoY; down QoQ vs ~INR 68 crore in Q4 FY26 (analyst-cited, not disputed)
Grew 66% YoY per management; analyst noted EBITDA margin declined QoQ
Management stated increase; exact YoY figure garbled in transcript

financial_highlights.value: About 17-18% (analyst's figure, not confirmed by management)
About INR 19 crore (analyst read) vs ~INR 2 crore last year

financial_highlights.metric: Changes in inventories / stock in trade
financial_highlights.value: About INR 17 crore vs ~INR 2 crore prior-year quarter
financial_highlights.change: Hardware for turnkey projects, recognised on milestones

segments.name: Domestic TSP / banking
segments.commentary: Remains the largest contributor; management expects its share to decline as other businesses grow faster, while still growing in absolute terms.

segments.name: PPaaS (payment platform as a service)
segments.commentary: Projection cut to about 5% of revenue from about 90% earlier, to reduce risk; management says MDR on UPI could revive it.

segments.name: RegTech / AI risk intelligence
segments.commentary: Order from a large PSU picked up; cooperative-bank deals won; SaaS subscription planned for mid and small banks. Management says about 650 million transactions processed on the product at 98% accuracy.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue now coming in; first global account won in Q1; one telecom super-app order in hand and two more deals in pipeline. Management expects margins above 35% vs 15-20% domestic.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of 60-70% YoY reiterated; management indicated about INR 320-340 crore for the year, which analyst Preet Shah stated and management called 'around that'.
FY27 EBITDA margin of around 30% reiterated; management says Q1 and Q2 orders should lift the blended margin later in the year.
Management targets 60-70% annual growth CAGR for the next 2-3 years, implying about INR 850-900 crore revenue by FY29 (per analyst calculation; management said 'tentatively yes').
International share targeted at about 30% in FY28-29 per Ashish Aggarwal and around 50% or more in about two years per Deepak Thakur; EBITDA margin target of at least 35% in about two years.
IPO funds: management expects deployment to start within the next two quarters, mainly product development and three shortlisted opportunities (RegTech, AI solutions, payment infrastructure).
Management said growth will come on a yearly basis and sequential revenue will be milestone-driven; no quarterly phasing given.
capex_capacity: Implementation cycle for international orders runs about 4 to 9 months; full project tenure 4-5 years or longer, with margins rising as milestones complete.
Investments in product, global business development, AI, SaaS infrastructure and skill revival are being made and are expensed, weighing on current margins.
Management says it is moving to an AI-driven organisation, targeting about 30% efficiency gain (per investor presentation); employee cost growth lagged revenue growth.
No specific capacity or capex figures were disclosed.
demand_pricing: UPI MDR: Parliament reportedly approved MDR on UPI; management says benefits are expected but no regulator, NPCI or bank guidance has been issued, so no numbers are being given. Management expects direct revenue from acquiring-platform contracts and indirect benefit via TSP spend.
Management said MDR on high-ticket UPI transactions (about 4-6% of volume, mostly large merchants) would be far below card MDR, so merchant shift to UPI is expected; no quantified impact.
Competition: established RegTech products (EFRM, EWS) face competition; management says its AI risk-intelligence product has no direct competitor yet.
Domestic margin 15-20% vs international 30-40%, as stated by management.
Acquisitions: priority is geographic access, product gaps and growth; no timeline (Q2 'early'). Management said growth is not inorganic.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue fell QoQ in Q1 versus 15-20% QoQ growth guidance; is FY27 guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 60-70% annual growth is unchanged; PPaaS cut to about 5% and milestone timing makes quarterly numbers lumpy; Q4 FY26 at about INR 68 crore is the peak to beat.

qa_highlights.question: How will MDR on UPI benefit the company, directly or indirectly?
qa_highlights.answer: Two routes: indirect (more bank and PSP money for TSP upgrades) and direct (per-transaction revenue on acquiring platforms it deployed). No numbers given until regulator, NPCI or bank guidance is out.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst estimate of MDR quantum (about INR 90,000 crore on 5% of volume at 0.25%).
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quote a number, saying MDR has acquiring, interchange and switching components, and the revenue stack is not yet clear.

qa_highlights.question: International orders, margin and mix target?
qa_highlights.answer: International is 10-12% of revenue; target about 30% in FY28-29 and about 50% in two years; margin 30-40% vs 15-20% domestic. Three first orders, one from a PSP, others from other segments.

qa_highlights.question: Deployment of IPO funds (about 10-15% used).
qa_highlights.answer: Three opportunities identified (RegTech, AI solutions, payment infrastructure); deployment expected to start in the next two quarters, mostly product development.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise to about INR 19 crore while employee cost stayed flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said purchase cost was grouped into other expenses, so the real other-expense line is about INR 2 crore; employee cost is less tied to revenue due to AI adoption.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 60-70% growth CAGR inclusive of inorganic growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not inorganic.

risks_watch: Lumpy, milestone-based revenue makes QoQ comparisons weak; Q1 was below Q4 FY26's INR 68 crore peak.
FY27 guidance needs about INR 260-280 crore over the remaining three quarters (analyst math), an average of about INR 90 crore a quarter versus INR 61 crore in Q1.
MDR on UPI is unquantified and depends on regulator, NPCI and bank directions; management says no numbers should be relied on.
Slow IPO fund deployment (about 10-15% used after about 8 months).
International ramp depends on 4-9 month implementation cycles; only one order in hand.
Opaque P&L grouping (purchase cost in other expenses) limits margin analysis; management reclassified the line.
